comments.body:
PHASE 1 RCA — Ubuntu runner occupancy (2026-08-13)

Baseline and attribution
- GitHub Actions run 31752047186: workflow wall 27m46s. macOS default remains the completion critical path at 22m15s. Ubuntu default cells were py3.11=615s, py3.12=634s, py3.13=563s: 1,812 runner-seconds (30.2 runner-minutes) per Verified run. Ubuntu integration cells were 81/92/81s and complexity-lock invocations were 52/54/55s. Other >30s Ubuntu operations: optional-extras isolate 91s and tickets-history mount 39s. No individual integration test exceeded 30s.
- Individual >30s Ubuntu tests/fixtures: bridge cadence 130.59/110.97/100.66s and AST provenance fixture setup 46.95/49.02/48.84s.

Confirmed mechanisms and discriminating experiments
1. Bridge cadence — tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py:164-184 calls _bridge_schedule() inside the 1,440-minute comprehension, so the same workflow YAML is read and parsed 1,440 times. Local median current=7.925s; read+parse=7.653s; parse preloaded text=7.584s; reuse one parsed schedule=0.00106s; cached schedule while retaining all 1,440 checks=0.000383s. This kills the hypothesis that exhaustive minute arithmetic is expensive: YAML parsing is the cost. Introduced by 432a92c165; prior 2b136e74e7 loaded once. Estimated Ubuntu saving from the measured CI cells is 342.22s / 5.70 runner-minutes per Verified run. Defect legitimacy: the existing test contract requires exhaustive uniform-cadence proof, not repeated I/O; hoisting restores the earlier invariant-loading pattern without changing any checked minute.
2. render_unit existential assertion — tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py:308-325 calls real Pandoc for all 232 eligible prose units, but asserts only eligible>0 and changed>0. Current=7.887s and 232 subprocesses. Exact short-circuit evaluation reaches both witnesses in 0.035s with 1 subprocess. Forced identity-renderer and no-eligible mutations fail identically under both forms, so this preserves the assertion and is not minute/content sampling.
3. Pandoc hardening oracle — tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py:65-98 and :440-458 executes both current _convert and a copied _legacy_convert for all 884 units. Combined corpus+hardening under -n4 invoked Pandoc 3,421 times (workers 890/652/974/905); wall 45.60s, user 45.02s, sys 50.77s. Corpus alone=29.52s; hardening alone=18.80s. Serial conversion median=33ms, p95=35.6ms, max=70.6ms, so aggregate process startup dominates. Cross-worker pass-1 sharing is working; duplicate cache fill is not the cause. Mutating shared _PANDOC_TO to plain kept current and copied legacy in agreement for all 884 units, proving the live-vs-live oracle is coupled. A static immutable expected baseline detected 799/884 such mutations while continuing to run product _convert through real Pandoc for every unit. Safe immediate repair: replace only the duplicated legacy subprocess side with immutable expected outputs; keep all 884 live product conversions. Full per-change substitution of real Pandoc conflicts with accepted ADR 0095 (every conversion assertion uses the real binary), so that broader option remains in architecture RESEARCH and requires explicit acknowledgment/supersession before drafting or implementation.
4. AST provenance setup — the three Ubuntu cells spend 46.95/49.02/48.84s in setup. Parsing is already cached by closed analogical-dashing-fennecfox. Focused local setup=3.37s; cProfile records ~9.54M ast.walk iterations and ~130.9M calls. The fixture repeatedly rediscovers enclosing callers and parent relationships. Build caller/parent indices once per process while preserving the exact 24 (key, expr, verdict) tuples and all existing guards.
5. Complexity lock — .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:449-455 runs the same OS/Python-invariant static policy in every matrix cell (Ubuntu 52/54/55s; macOS 45s). Move one invocation into the existing lint job and delete four duplicates. Estimated net saving ~154 runner-seconds / 2.57 runner-minutes per Verified run; coverage is unchanged because the policy is evaluated once on the same commit.
6. Jira DC — Verified uses -m "not integration and not external". tests/external/live_jira_dc collects zero tests in Verified (62 deselected); the weekly/manual external harness runs 63 tests and takes 2,384–2,635s. It is already outside the hot path, so moving it saves exactly 0 seconds. Jira/DC-oriented hermetic unit files provide the smaller substitute already: 472 passed in 6.67s under -n4, slowest 0.76s. Removing them would save only seconds and reduce coverage.
7. Mutation testing — from closed cryptic-damp-panda: 62 successful post-addition runs, only 5 selected mutation shards, and mutation was never the last prerequisite, so measured completion-path addition=0. Selector-only cost ~0.42 runner-min/run. Selected mutation averages ~50.1 runner-min and can contribute contention, but it does not explain the observed completion-latency regression.

OSS consensus and tracker checks
- Hoist/share invariants: pytest uses session-scoped invariant fixtures; Django uses setUpTestData; Pylint/Astroid precedent is recorded on analogical-dashing-fennecfox.
- Existential short-circuit: pytest testing/test_nodes.py, Django tests/asgi/tests.py, and CPython importlib metadata tests use any(...).
- Static/golden oracle paired with live implementation: Pandoc test/Tests/Writers/Jira.hs uses literal expected writer output; Kubernetes client-go/dynamic/golden_test.go uses committed fixtures; Rust compiletest uses blessed .stderr/.stdout fixtures.
- Small real boundary plus fast substitutes: nbconvert and pypandoc use small real Pandoc contracts; OpenTofu mock_provider, Kubernetes fake clientsets/httptest, and pycontribs/jira requests_mock keep routine checks hermetic.
- Static policy once outside language matrices: CPython lint.yml, Django linters.yml, and Rust/Kubernetes tidy/verify surfaces.
All surveyed projects were active on 2026-08-12/13; popularity: Pandoc 45.8k, Rust 115k, Kubernetes 124k, pytest 14.4k, Django 88.4k, CPython 74.3k, OpenTofu 29.8k, nbconvert 1.9k, pypandoc 1.1k, pycontribs/jira 2.1k stars. Each immediate remediation clears the ticket-defined >=2/3 consensus rule.
- Prior tickets searched: cryptic-damp-panda (original RCA), harmless-wavy-osprey (xdist sharing), albinic-agrologic-dolphin and ashy-waterlog-hamadryas (Pandoc hardening), analogical-dashing-fennecfox (first AST cache), humble-cinnamoned-mussel (complexity merge-base correctness), coercive-paediatric-bug (rejects extra sharding/workers without aggregate savings), dimmed-supersweet-xenarthra (deferred production Pandoc spawn-cost idea). No rejection found for schedule hoisting, exact existential short-circuiting, immutable legacy oracle, AST indexing, or one-time complexity invocation.

Phase-1 conclusion
The proven Ubuntu levers are redundant work, not reduced coverage or added parallelism. Proceed on separate linked implementation tickets for the five consensus-backed repairs. Jira routing needs no change. Full static substitution for all Pandoc conversion assertions is held at architecture RESEARCH because it would supersede ADR 0095.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
The completed Gerrit Verified latency RCA optimized the macOS completion path, but Ubuntu jobs still occupy scarce org-wide runners for 11-14 minutes and contribute to queue contention. Follow-up questions identify three candidate levers: replace repeated Pandoc corpus rendering with static expected results plus a smaller boundary test, remove redundant work from the exhaustive 1,440-minute bridge cadence proof, and determine whether expensive Jira DC-oriented default-tier tests can move out of the per-change hot path while retaining fast unit coverage. The genuinely live tests/external/live_jira_dc suite is already excluded from Gerrit Verified by the `not external` selector and runs in its dedicated harness; moving that suite again would save zero. This work must preserve behavioral coverage and must not use extra parallel jobs or unchanged aggregate runner usage.

## Plan
- Build a dated Ubuntu runner-time dossier from final post-remediation run 31752047186, pytest duration logs, workflow routing, and focused local runtime experiments.
- For Pandoc and render_unit, map every current assertion to the code boundary it exercises. Include both full-corpus consumers: test_wiki_render_corpus.py (~884 pass-1 subprocesses plus additional passes) and test_wiki_render_hardening.py (~1,768 subprocesses for byte-equivalence). Compare static golden fixtures, a bounded real-Pandoc contract sample, and full-corpus external execution using defect-seeded experiments to detect any coverage loss. Treat the pinned Pandoc-version-to-output coupling as an explicit external boundary. Any accepted golden fixture must identify its Pandoc version and binary fingerprint, provide a documented regeneration command, and include a fast drift assertion that fails when the installed Pandoc version differs. The full real-Pandoc corpus must remain in the scheduled external-integration workflow as the revalidation destination, including after pin changes.
- For the bridge cadence test, discriminate between the cost of the 1,440 arithmetic checks and invariant workflow YAML I/O; prefer hoisting invariant I/O if it preserves the exhaustive proof.
- Confirm the live Jira DC suite routing, then inventory the Jira DC-oriented harness-free tests that actually execute in the default tier. Identify which, if any, exercise a genuine external boundary rather than our code, and map any proposed lane move to faster existing or new unit contracts before implementation.
- Compare each candidate with current practice in at least three named, popular, actively maintained OSS projects. Consensus means at least two-thirds of the surveyed projects, rounded up, use the practice and no surveyed project documents rejecting it for coverage or reliability; otherwise route the proposal to operator disposition.
- Search tracker history for prior acceptance or rejection of every proposal.
- Measure deterministic savings with paired before/after runs under the same environment. Report per-cell elapsed-time delta, sum the deltas across the three Ubuntu Python cells as runner-minutes freed per Verified run, and report the baseline-normalized Ubuntu occupancy reduction as `sum(cell deltas) / sum(baseline cell durations)`. This occupancy metric is the queue-pressure capacity effect; do not infer queue-wait reduction from one run. If GitHub job records expose queued/start timestamps for a multi-run sample, report the observed wait distribution separately with sample size and confidence, without attributing causality.
- Record a confirmed RCA and measured runner-time/wall-time savings. Create linked implementation tickets only for remediations that preserve coverage; under the operator standing approval, implement those meeting the defined OSS-consensus bar through Gerrit. Back-out for any merged CI behavior change is a Gerrit revert restoring the prior full per-change execution; the scheduled full-corpus lane remains available as the coverage oracle during diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every Ubuntu operation or test phase over 30 seconds in the final sample is attributed to a specific mechanism and measured with a focused baseline.
- [ ] The Pandoc corpus proposal covers both full-corpus consumers and has an assertion-level coverage map plus A/B runtime estimate.
- [ ] The render_unit proposal has an assertion-level coverage map and A/B runtime estimate.
- [ ] The bridge-cadence proposal has an assertion-level coverage map and A/B runtime estimate.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The live Jira DC routing is recorded with workflow citations.
- [ ] The default-tier Jira DC-oriented proposal has an assertion-level coverage map and A/B runtime estimate.
- [ ] Each proposal cites tracker history.
- [ ] Each proposal cites at least three named popular actively maintained OSS projects and applies the defined consensus rule.
- [ ] No accepted remediation removes an assertion, behavioral equivalence class, OS/Python cell, or external boundary.
- [ ] Every moved coverage boundary has an explicit destination and schedule.
- [ ] Every accepted golden fixture identifies the exact Pandoc version and binary fingerprint that produced it.
- [ ] Every accepted golden fixture includes a documented runnable regeneration command.
- [ ] Every accepted golden fixture has a fast automated version-drift assertion and a scheduled full real-Pandoc revalidation lane.
- [ ] Runner-minute savings are quantified without counting parallel matrix time as critical-path wall time.
- [ ] Queue-pressure capacity savings are reported as runner-minutes freed per run and baseline-normalized Ubuntu occupancy reduction; any observed queue-wait distribution is reported separately and not presented as causal.
- [ ] Every consensus-backed remediation is implemented on a linked ticket.
- [ ] Every implemented remediation passes repository gates and Gerrit LLM-Review +1 plus Verified +1 before merge.
- [ ] Every implemented remediation merges before this task closes.
- [ ] Non-consensus or coverage-risking proposals are summarized with evidence and left for operator disposition.
- [ ] The back-out path for each merged remediation is recorded as a Gerrit revert restoring full per-change execution.
compiled_state.no_file_impact_reason: Phase 1 is a read-only CI investigation; any accepted implementation will use a separate linked ticket with explicit file impact.
compiled_state.title: Reduce Ubuntu CI runner occupancy without losing test coverage
